title: Programmable remodelling of carbon–nitrogen connectivity in amines
excerpt: Tertiary amines are ubiquitous motifs in biologically active molecules, where they play central roles in molecular recognition and function1,2. Among these, tertiary benzylamines are particularly prominent in discovery chemistry as readily assembled starting points for lead generation from abundant building blocks3,4, with favourable physicochemical and binding properties. However, despite their accessibility, the core C–N connectivity of these frameworks remains effectively locked5,6, confining diversification to benzylamine derivatives and preventing direct access to structurally distinct aryl–alkylamine architectures. Overcoming this limitation requires direct and selective reconfiguration of C–N connectivity within fully elaborated amine scaffolds. Here we show that tertiary benzylamines can be transformed from static scaffolds into programmable platforms for molecular diversification through catalytic remodeling of their C–N bonds7-9. N-alkylation with a bifunctional electrophile generates a quaternary ammonium intermediate that encodes palladium-catalyzed disassembly and reconfiguration of C–N connectivity. This concept is first exemplified through one-carbon homologation of tertiary benzylamines and, more significantly, establishes a general strategy for programmable insertion of modular units—ranging from single carbon atoms to complex molecular fragments, including hydrocarbon chains, heterocycles and aryl groups—directly across the C–N bond on fully elaborated amine scaffolds. This capability opens a route to programmable diversification of amine frameworks, enabling systematic exploration of amine connectivity and molecular architecture.

Abstract

Tertiary amines are ubiquitous motifs in biologically active molecules, where they play central roles in molecular recognition and function1,2. Among these, tertiary benzylamines are particularly prominent in discovery chemistry as readily assembled starting points for lead generation from abundant building blocks3,4, with favourable physicochemical and binding properties. However, despite their accessibility, the core C–N connectivity of these frameworks remains effectively locked5,6, confining diversification to benzylamine derivatives and preventing direct access to structurally distinct aryl–alkylamine architectures. Overcoming this limitation requires direct and selective reconfiguration of C–N connectivity within fully elaborated amine scaffolds. Here we show that tertiary benzylamines can be transformed from static scaffolds into programmable platforms for molecular diversification through catalytic remodeling of their C–N bonds7-9. N-alkylation with a bifunctional electrophile generates a quaternary ammonium intermediate that encodes palladium-catalyzed disassembly and reconfiguration of C–N connectivity. This concept is first exemplified through one-carbon homologation of tertiary benzylamines and, more significantly, establishes a general strategy for programmable insertion of modular units—ranging from single carbon atoms to complex molecular fragments, including hydrocarbon chains, heterocycles and aryl groups—directly across the C–N bond on fully elaborated amine scaffolds. This capability opens a route to programmable diversification of amine frameworks, enabling systematic exploration of amine connectivity and molecular architecture.

抽象的

叔胺是生物活性分子中普遍存在的基序，在分子识别和功能中发挥着核心作用1,2。 其中，叔苄胺在发现化学中特别突出，作为从丰富的结构单元3,4生成先导化合物的容易组装的起点，具有良好的物理化学和结合特性。 然而，尽管它们具有可访问性，但这些框架的核心 C-N 连接仍然有效地锁定5,6，限制了苄胺衍生物的多样化，并阻止直接访问结构不同的芳基-烷基胺结构。 克服这一限制需要在精心设计的胺支架内直接和选择性地重新配置 C-N 连接。 在这里，我们展示了叔苄胺可以从静态支架转变为可编程平台，通过其 C-N 键的催化重塑来实现分子多样化7-9。 用双功能亲电子试剂进行 N-烷基化会生成季铵中间体，该中间体编码钯催化的 C-N 连接分解和重构。 这个概念首先通过叔苄胺的一碳同系化得到例证，更重要的是，建立了一种模块化单元可编程插入的通用策略——从单个碳原子到复杂的分子片段，包括烃链、杂环和芳基——直接穿过完全精心设计的胺支架上的C-N键。 这种能力为胺框架的可编程多样化开辟了道路，从而能够系统地探索胺连接性和分子结构。
